(1) the performance of a Reading Comprehension model depends on the choice of word embedding method, (2) a good embedding method is one that is pre-trained on a large corpus of text, and (3) a good embedding is one that is able to capture semantic information, not just syntactic information.

(1) the choice of pre-trained word embedding is more important than the architecture, (2) pre-trained embeddings should be used, even when they are not fine-tuned, (3) the use of a pre-trained language model (ELMo, BERT, or RoBERTa) as a word embedding is the best choice, and (4) a simple heuristic for handling out-of-vocabulary tokens at testing time is to replace them with the average of their in-vocabulary neighbors.

the question: what are the key design decisions in a Reading Comprehension system, and how do they affect the final performance?
the question: what are the best practices for word embeddings in Reading Comprehension?
